title: Palak Paneer
subtitle: Punjabi spinach curry with fresh cheese
excerpt: The classic Punjabi vegetarian curry: blanched spinach blended to a vivid green purée with ginger and spices, then simmered with pan-fried cubes of paneer until the sauce is silky and the cheese has absorbed the flavours of the gravy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Palak paneer (spinach with paneer) is one of the most widely eaten vegetarian dishes in north Indian cooking, particularly associated with Punjab. Palak means spinach; saag is sometimes used interchangeably but technically refers to a mixture of leafy greens (mustard greens, spinach, fenugreek) that produces a more pungent and rustic result. The dish uses paneer, a fresh, firm, unsalted Indian curd cheese that does not melt when heated, making it ideal for simmering in sauces. The spinach is blanched briefly to preserve its bright colour, then blended to a smooth purée. The paneer is usually pan-fried until golden before adding, which improves its texture. A small amount of cream or butter added at the end gives the sauce its characteristic richness.

content.text: Blanch and cool the spinach in ice water to preserve its bright green colour; this step makes the visual difference between vivid green and a murky khaki. Fry the paneer until golden before adding to the sauce; raw paneer added directly will be soft and bland.

items.preparation: baby or regular spinach; blanched in boiling water for 1 minute, refreshed in ice water, drained

content.text: Blend the drained blanched spinach with 4 tablespoons of water to a smooth purée. Set aside. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the paneer cubes until golden on two sides, about 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.

Heat the remaining oil in the pan. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they splutter. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes and ground spices and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down.

Add the spinach purée and salt. Stir to combine. Add the paneer and 100 ml of water. Simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the cream and garam masala. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with naan or chapati and rice.
